text: It goes in a straight line until something stops it. Over the acid, a number of things stop it. I had them put there.
The light does not mind where you are standing when it moves. Find out whether you do.
The crate is smaller than you are. I mention it because the building was designed by someone who had noticed.
That white drip is primer. One coat, and bare board takes a portal. You have just watched it do the floor.
The rest of the bare board is across the acid. The primer is not. I would call that an oversight, but I signed the drawing.
Paint goes where it is thrown, and it stays there. Choose your first wall the way you would choose a tattoo.
The buttons are slow to wake and quick to sleep. You are the other way round. Plan accordingly.
This chamber uses everything so far: the cube, the light, the field, and a sentry, who has been waiting.
The field forgets your portals for you. It is the only thing in this building with a shorter memory than yours.

The amber plate runs the pump. Step on it again and the pump runs the other way. The door over there wants a weight, and the field recycles anything you carry. I do enjoy it when the rules agree with each other.
Your passenger will spend the whole voyage looking at whatever you were looking at when you said goodbye. Choose it a view.
You are in a storeroom that is not on my plans. I have excellent plans. I am going to look at them again until you come out.
The crate is in the cell on the island. It has been there since the last subject left it there. They are not there. Draw whatever conclusion keeps you moving.
The doorway has a field in it. Fields do not like portals, and they do not like luggage. They are indifferent to you. We have that in common.
Things that cannot leave by the door have been known to leave by the wall. I am not suggesting anything. I am a ceiling.
You retrieved it. One crate, slightly travelled. I will put it back on the island for the next subject, when there is one.
There is a room up there. There has always been a room up there. I simply chose not to mention it, or light it, or know about it.
Nine lasers, three sentries, one crate and a launch pad. I call it a gauntlet. The sentries call it lunch.
Everything in this room has been explained to you at least once. I am therefore not going to explain any of it. Consider that a compliment, if it helps.
The pad does not care what it throws. One of you is more durable than the other. I will let you work out which.
You ran the gauntlet. It ran out of ideas before you did. That has not happened before, and I would like it not to happen again.
